help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file that had already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing is started. The service and source shown remain the current ones, and next to the service name a message indicates where the file will go, for example Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces it; choosing the source already in use removes it. After you resume, it changes to show Switching to … until the switch takes effect and then disappears. If a download's paused files go to different places, or if the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over, so its new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service during the pause works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take over the link in use takes over immediately (the indicator shows this), and one that first needs to prepare a copy shows Preparing … and only takes over after you resume. These messages appear in the Download activity and Downloads rows; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has the option Prepare backup torrents. While it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is delivering, to be ready to take over if needed, and, when you switch a download to another service, the torrent it had already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first. Turn it off to keep that service's slots free for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. A choice you have already saved is kept.

help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.admin.backTranslation: An Admin can remove, cancel or switch the source of any download. help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If you add a magnet, a {file_type} file, NZB or Metalink that DebridPulse is already working on (including one that failed and was not removed), it shows Already in the queue and keeps the existing download instead of starting a second one. Web links are always added as a new download. After a download is completed, cancelled or removed, adding the same source again starts a new download. When two downloads end up fetching the same content, DebridPulse may merge them; the merged download shows Consolidated. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the merged download shows Consolidated · Unverified. Merging does not change who requested it: each account's request remains its own.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists each person with their role, how they sign in, and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user applies immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role, without ending their session. Each person has a DebridPulse username, separate from the display name: an OIDC account receives it from the first sign-in, and it is with this name that one signs in using a local password; the pencil next to it, in the Edit user title, changes this name and keeps any stored password. Click an account's name to see its details and activity, where a pending request can be withdrawn individually. Disable and Remove first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also requested continues, and completed downloads are never affected. Disabling also ends the account's sign-ins and stops its tokens; removing keeps the account's history and deletes its notification settings. A removed OIDC sign-in that signs in again receives a new account, which stays disabled until you enable it. Merge joins two or more accounts into the one you choose to keep; two accounts that share a verified email are flagged, but only a merge joins them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Admin, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

Restoring pauses processing, makes a safety backup of the current state, verifies the chosen backup again, replaces the current database and settings, and restarts the DebridPulse services. If the verification fails, nothing is changed, and all pauses that you or an *arr client had set go back to how they were.

The same section sets how often statistics snapshots are taken and how long they are kept: a record of the previous 24 hours of activity, saved in the DebridPulse database. DebridPulse always makes a safety backup first and cancels the operation if that backup fails. It stops the downloads in progress and pauses processing during the reset; afterwards, it restores the previous pause state. Files already completed in your downloads folder are not deleted.
